headline: Maui County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee
meeting.voteItem: Remove the word puʻuhonua from the bill
meeting.summary: The committee reviewed proposed changes to Bill 111 on removing and storing property in public places, then deferred it with no objections.
meeting.recap: The committee discussed Bill 111, which sets rules for removing and storing property in public places and creates a right to shelter.[[0:05:53]] A testifier strongly supported the bill's section on finding other shelter before a camp is removed.[[0:34:26]] The committee decided not to vote on changes today and to note only where members agreed.[[1:58:56]] Members agreed not to use the word puʻuhonua in the bill.[[2:13:03]] A resource person asked for an immediate moratorium, or pause, on sweeps (clearing of homeless camps).[[2:17:38]] The committee chose to revisit a proposal to cut the notice before a camp removal from 45 days to 14.[[2:29:45]] Members agreed an informational meeting must be held at the site at least four days before a removal.[[2:31:26]] Members agreed to drop a section that would let the Council set a fee for storing property.[[2:48:39]] The committee deferred the bill with no objections.[[2:56:30]]
decided: Members agreed by consensus not to use the word puʻuhonua in the bill.
Members agreed by consensus that notice photos be made available on request instead of posted on a County website.
Members agreed by consensus to require an informational meeting at the site at least four days before a removal.
Members agreed by consensus to drop the section allowing a fee for storing and recovering property.
meeting.next: The chair said the bill will come back at the next meeting with more chances for testimony. The committee will invite a County director to help define Hawaiian words used in the bill. The administration and outreach providers agreed to work together on the bill before the committee meets again.

moments.q: Testimony on the meaning of puʻuhonua
"I would like to request an immediate moratorium"

issues.brief: A testifier said a recent report found rents have gone up 44% since the fires.[[#1]] The administration proposed 14 days of notice before a camp removal instead of 45.[[#2]] Members agreed an informational meeting must be held at the site at least four days before a removal.[[#3]]
